name: Bird dog
movement: on all fours, one leg reached back and the opposite arm forward, level with the back, held and brought back

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: On all fours, one leg reached straight back and the opposite arm forward, level with the back, held.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Kneel on all fours side on to it, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.
words.position: Kneel on all fours side on to the phone, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat like a table top, eyes down.
words.top: One leg reached straight back and the opposite arm straight forward, both level with the back — the foot no higher than the hips — the back flat and the hips square to the floor.
howto: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat, head in line. Brace the stomach gently — stiffen, don’t hollow.
Reach one leg straight back, pushing through the heel, and the opposite arm straight forward until both are level with your back. No higher: the foot stays at hip height.
Hold for the count without the trunk moving and with the hips square — imagine a glass of water on your lower back.
Bring them back slowly to all fours. The rep counts there. Then the other side.
words.cannot: The hips rotating, the lower back arching and the head: it sees the leg and arm heights, the reaching knee and the hip-to-shoulder line from the side. Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor and your eyes to the floor yourself.
words.about: Bird dog — on all fours side on: the leg, as how far the hip-to-knee line is lifted from hanging straight down, 75–95° at the top (90 is level with the back; higher and the lower back arches to lift it); a rep is under way past 45 and counts when the knee is back under 20; the reaching knee at least 155°, the leg long; the opposite arm, shoulder to wrist, 70–110°, level; and the trunk, as the hip-to-shoulder line read against where it was at the start, within 8° either way — the chest dropping or the body rocking back. Hold six seconds at the top (McGill: no more than seven or eight). The leg lifted is the one measured, the opposite arm with it.
words.lost: Kneel on all fours side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it out there next time
words.safety: The back should feel nothing; if it does, lift less high or do the leg alone first.
words.easier: The leg alone, then the arm alone; a shorter hold; a lower reach.
words.harder: A longer hold, up to seven or eight seconds; sweep the hand and the knee lightly along the floor between reps instead of resting; make a fist with the reaching hand.
words.mistakes: Lifting the leg above the hips and arching the back; bending the reaching knee; the chest sinking into the supporting shoulder; rotating the hips open; looking up; rushing.

measurements.label: leg lifted
measurements.why: How far the hip-to-knee line is lifted from hanging straight down: 0 kneeling, 90 level with the back. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Leg lifted at the top, at least (90 is level)
Leg lifted at the top, at most

measurements.label: leg long

settings.label: Reaching knee, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The reaching leg's knee: the leg pushed long through the heel reads near 180; a bent knee lets the thigh look level without the reach.

measurements.label: opposite arm lifted
measurements.why: The far arm, shoulder to wrist, lifted from hanging: 90 is reaching straight forward, level. Not read when the far wrist is hidden.

settings.label: Arm lifted at the top, at least (90 is level)
Arm lifted at the top, at most

measurements.label: back off its start line
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line, as its change since the start: the chest sinking toward the supporting hand reads down, the body rocking back toward the heels reads up. There is no landmark on the lower back, so an arch is not seen — keep the leg at hip height and it does not come.

settings.label: Back within ± of its start line (degrees)

prompt.text: Reach the leg back and the opposite arm forward

faults.label: Leg short
faults.text: Reach the leg back until it is level

faults.label: Leg too high
faults.text: Not so high — the leg level with your back, no higher
faults.deep: The foot is above the hips — lower the leg to hip height

faults.label: Leg bent
faults.text: Straighten the leg — push the heel back

faults.label: Chest dropping
faults.text: Push the floor away — chest up
faults.deep: The chest is sinking toward the floor — push the floor away

faults.label: Rocking back
faults.text: Keep your trunk still — weight over hands and knees
